subject: DeltaOps post-upgrade spike: request for emergency rollback and exec attention
messages:
From: Suresh Patel <suresh@deltaops.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 24 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DeltaOps service: sudden latency & error spike after v3.2q rollout

Olga / Marissa,

We started seeing a major jump in tail latency and a small but consistent increase in model hallucinations right after your v3.2 + qprofile 'v3.2q-128' went live in our production pool at ~08:45 PDT. The p99 has moved from ~380ms to ~1.6s and error rate (502/timeout) is up ~3x. Attached is a CSV with sample bad responses and timestamps (samples_bad_responses.csv).

This is impacting our customer flows for invoice ingestion — samples show truncated JSON outputs and some unrelated text insertion. Can you confirm immediately whether this rollout touched our Dedicated pool and whether there is an emergency rollback option? We need a response within 2 hours.

Elena (ops) is looping in contracts/finance if we need credits or formal downtime windows.

--
Suresh Patel
CTO, DeltaOps
suresh@deltaops.com
+1 415-555-0123
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Suresh Patel <suresh@deltaops.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 24 Jun 2028 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DeltaOps service: sudden latency & error spike after v3.2q rollout

Thanks Suresh — really sorry you're seeing this. We're pulling logs and tracing now. Can you confirm the first impacted timestamp you saw and whether you were hitting a pinned model variant or the routed pool? Any recent config changes on your side?

I've opened an internal incident and attached our initial trace request (deltaops_trace.zip). Looping in Rishi and Jonas from Serving to triage. We'll report back within 45 minutes with a mitigation plan (rollback vs profile tweak).

Action items for Redwood:
- Confirm which quant profile was applied to your pool and whether the canary completed.
- Gather p50/p95/p99 token-level timings and recent kube pod restarts.
- Surface any decode stalls or kernel fallback logs.

--
Olga Petrov
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 24 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DeltaOps service: sudden latency & error spike after v3.2q rollout

On Sun, Jun 24, 2028 at 09:28 AM olga.petrov@redwood.ai wrote:
> I've opened an internal incident and attached our initial trace request (deltaops_trace.zip).

Quick update from runtime — correlating your provided timestamps with our metrics: p99 CPU/GPU scheduling latency jumped concurrent with the quantizing of the model weights in the pool. We see a mix of two issues: increased decode time for long sequences (tokenization interaction with qprofile) and sporadic kernel fallback on a subset of nodes that causes 1.2s+ stalls. Attached: p99_profiles.pdf and runtime-metrics.csv.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: the v3.2q-128 quant profile changed the activation packing that our optimized kernel expects; on some GPU/driver combos that triggers a slower fallback path. Not all hosts are affected — it's a sampling/dispatcher routing problem.

Immediate options (pros/cons):
1) Emergency rollback to fp16 v3.2 across your Dedicated pool (fastest, restores latency but increases cost).
2) Narrow rollout: pin traffic to the small set of hosts that passed the canary (low risk but complex routing change).
3) Patch qprofile (longer) and redeploy canary.

Recommend option 1 while we prepare a narrow routing fix. I'll prepare the rollback runbook now.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Subject: URGENT: Approval needed for emergency rollback (DeltaOps - DLT-421)

Team —

DeltaOps is requesting an emergency rollback of the quant profile that shipped yesterday. Rishi's team recommends rolling back the Dedicated pool to fp16 v3.2 immediately (option 1) to restore p99 latency. This will increase our cost for DeltaOps' traffic while the fallback is active and we may need to issue a credit.

Requesting:
- Exec sign-off for emergency rollback and a one-time credit up to $10k if SLA thresholds are missed.
- Legal/Finance to acknowledge receipt of PO_update.pdf and confirm any procurement constraints on rollback timing (contracts@redwood.ai is on copy).

Impact summary:
- Estimated mitigation timeline: 30–45 minutes from approval.
- Expected p99 restoration to ~380–420ms; decode-quality to prior baseline.
- Cost delta: +18% until qprofile issue is fully resolved.

I'll coordinate the rollback once we have approval. Suresh & Elena have requested written confirmation and a DocuSign rollback acknowledgement; link included in related_links.

--
Olga Petrov
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: URGENT: Approval needed for emergency rollback (DeltaOps - DLT-421)

Confirmed — rollback scheduled and will start at 18:05 PDT (18:05:00 -07:00). Runbook attached (rollback_runbook.md). Steps:
1) Withdraw qprofile assignment from DeltaOps pool.
2) Re-point traffic to fp16 v3.2 variant with traffic draining (5s grace).
3) Monitor p50/p95/p99 for first 10 minutes; abort and escalate if errors > 2% or p99 > 800ms.
4) Post-mortem scheduled for 2028-06-28 09:00 PDT.

Rishi will own live metrics, I'll handle the routing change, and Olga/Marissa will manage customer comms and credit note.

Jonas
